subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw add native backup exclude-pattern controls now, and if so which defaults, protected paths, and exclude-file behavior should be part of the core CLI contract?
rationale: The missing capability is clear from source, but the final behavior decides the balance between archive size, sensitive-file avoidance, and restorable backups; automation should not choose that product/security policy while the linked PR is under review.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, security review, and real proof before landing or narrowing it.

options.title: Narrow to explicit custom excludes
options.body: Accept only `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` first while deferring smart defaults until restore completeness and security expectations are clearer.

options.title: Decline native excludes for now
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document the current scope, and direct optional backup strategies to plugin/ClawHub paths after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, security review, and real proof before landing or narrowing it.

likelyOwner.reason: gumadeiras is the strongest original backup-contract review signal from the feature history and is well placed to decide the restore-safety boundary.
